title: US Department of Housing and Urban Development /Mixed-Status Families Rule / Change Longstanding Federal Housing Policy by Restricting Assistance to Mixed-Status Families and Imposing Additional Citizenship and Immigration Status Verification Requirements on Residents Receiving Federal Housing
motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department (LARD), with the assistance of the Community Investment Department (CID), and the City Administrative Officer (CAO), and request the Housing Authority of the City of Los Angeles (HACLA) and the City Attorney, as appropriate, to prepare a report with recommendations on the anticipated impacts of the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development's (HUD) recently enacted Mixed-Status Families Rule, including but not limited to, the following: • An assessment of the number of households and individuals potentially impacted by the rule, including mixed-status families, with a breakdown by Council District, where available, and consistent with applicable privacy protections, including households with seniors aged 62 and older, individuals with disabilities, and residents living on fixed mcomes. • An analysis of the potential impacts on housing stability, including households at risk of losing federal housing assistance, possible evictions, family separation, and increased homelessness, as well as anticipated implementation and compliance timelines, including potential increases in senior homelessness, impacts on emergency and transitional shelter capacity, and increased demand for the City's FamilySource and Survivor Services systems, as well as barriers older adults may face in meeting new federal verification requirements) • An assessment of the anticipated financial and administrative costs to HACLA, participating housing providers, and the City, including eligibility verification, HOUSING administrative processing, housing displacement, and increased demand for homelessness prevention services. • An evaluation of applicable federal, state, and local legal protections, and legal remedies available to affected residents. An identification of existing City, County, and non-federal funding sources and programs that could provide emergency rental assistance and other housing stabilization services to prevent displacement. • A coordinated strategy that includes public policies/ ordinances that the City can adopt to provide timely, accessible, and multilingual information to potentially affected residents regarding the rule's requirements, applicable deadlines, tenant rights, available legal assistance, and housing stabilization resources, to prevent unnecessary housing displacement resulting from misinformation or confusion, and thereby potentially exacerbating the homeless crisis. < 0 PRESENTED BY: c/4d4~ IMELDA PADILLA llt~1 r· . fl{ i: November 17, 2026

departments: Housing Authority of the City of Los Angeles
requests.asks: Anticipated impacts of HUD's Mixed-Status Families Rule on affected households, housing stability, City and HACLA costs, legal protections and remedies, available funding sources, and a coordinated multilingual public information strategy, with recommendations.
